title: Trail and Monsoon
premise: Storm chaser Ulyana Oyelaran, deep in debt to the Vantablack Syndicate's cheerful enforcers, is salvaging flood debris along a glacial river when she recovers a chest bearing the seal of Kestria, a nation erased from maps forty years ago. The chest points to a wrecked diplomatic barge sealed inside a glacier, holding proof of who betrayed Kestria — and a claim that could clear her debts or bury her. Racing a salvage fleet and the six tides before calving season opens the ice route, Ulyana must decide whether justice belongs to survivors or to the law that abandoned them. In the end she floods the evidence to the world instead of selling it, pays her debt with the truth, and finds belonging not in a restored nation but in the crew that chose to stay with her.
about_author: E. M. Villalobos is a former river guide who spent six seasons in glacial outwash country before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people the map forgot.

chapters.title: Debt of Weather
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Chasing a storm for contract footage to pay the Syndicate, she loses her drone and nearly her truck, then faces her creditors' smiling deadline: sixty days. Emotional beat: exhaustion sharpened into defiance; she takes one last salvage job upriver rather than surrender her rig.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, with crewmate Dev interludes. Dredging after a flood surge, they haul up a lead-lined chest stamped with Kestria's extinct double-star seal, containing a manifest naming a barge lost inside the Meridian Glacier. Beat: wonder curdling into fear as she realizes what it's worth and to whom.

chapters.title: The Optimists Call
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The Syndicate's envoy, Mr. Fenn, offers to forgive everything if she delivers the chest's contents exclusively — while a rival salvage fleet, hired by Kestrian exiles, shadows her camp. Beat: the trap of being wanted by everyone and owned by no one.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The crew calculates the route: only six tidal surges will raise the outflow enough to reach the ice cave before calving season seals it. One crewmember walks, taking a copy of the manifest to sell. Beat: loyalty tested by arithmetic.

chapters.title: Country of Ice
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The ascent through moraine and meltwater; a near-fatal crevasse crossing forces trust between Ulyana and the exiles' scout, Ilma, who reveals the barge carried Kestria's last legitimate government-in-exile records. Beat: grief for a homeland neither of them can return to.

chapters.title: The Fleet at the Moraine
chapters.summary: Ilma's POV. The rival fleet camps within sight; sabotage cuts their anchor lines, and Ulyana saves a drowning rival skipper instead of letting the river take him. Beat: mercy as strategy and as identity — justice outside the law begins here.

chapters.title: Third Tide, Rising
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Inside the blue ice tunnel they find the barge, half-crushed, its strongbox intact — and evidence that the betrayal was brokered by the very state that now licenses the salvage fleet. Beat: revelation; the race was never about treasure but testimony.

chapters.title: Calving
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The glacier begins to fail early; Fenn arrives by air with Syndicate muscle and a court order claiming the wreck. In the chaos, the fifth tide traps the fleet's lead vessel. Beat: panic, sacrifice — Ilma stays behind to free the trapped rivals.

chapters.title: The Weight of Proof
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. With one tide left, Fenn offers her debt-free life for the strongbox. She broadcasts the documents via satellite instead, giving them to every exile network at once so no buyer can own them. Beat: climax — choosing the world over her own rescue.

chapters.title: After the Water
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, closing with Ilma's letter. The Syndicate settles cheaply rather than face exposure; Kestrians begin restitution proceedings using her broadcast. Ulyana, broke again but unowned, watches the first tide of the new season with her remaining crew. Beat: belonging found in chosen company, not inherited nations.
